page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page, p. 481 of the book). Running head at the top. Below it a centred two-line title, "HISTORIA IMPLEMENTI.", then one column of running text with a decorated initial at the start. No marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right, signature at the foot.

main_text.head: HISTORIA IMPLEMENTI.
main_text.p: §. 1. L[?]icet nondum omnium rerum cernamus finem, ac nesciamus quid serus advecturus sit vesper, nisi in quantum nobis aliqua futurorum spes facta est per scripturas propheticas: nihilominus hic loci quaedam notanda sunt, ut hactenus per historiam Novi Testamenti confirmata.

1. Videas hic ut errorem notari sententiam de usu simulacrorum Doctrinali, atque quosdam hic repraesentari sub N. Test. ab errore revocandos. Praevidit itaque in spiritu Propheta simulacra in ecclesiam introducenda, & sub hoc colore à quibusdam retinenda. Nec vana fuit illa praevisio: quam primum enim à simplicitate primitivae trium anteriorum seculorum ecclesiae (quae nulla admisit in ecclesiis simulacra, ut à variis demonstratum est) inceperunt recedere Christiani, & in sacris divitias ostentare pace Constantini acquisitas, augusta sacris condita sunt templa, & pretiosa quaesita ornamenta, peristromata nempe, & vela, quandoquidem acupicta, quae spontaneorum munificentia liberali manu attulit. Cumque inter ea in Hispania maturè etiam picturae numerarentur, cavit Concilium Eliberitanum picturas reciperent aut admitterent: ita enim praecipit canon istius Conc. 36. page.notes: The decorated initial is a large ornamental letter; the first letter is likely L (Licet), marked [?]. The "1." before "Videas" is a printed paragraph number and is kept in the text. Long s is written as plain s throughout. The line "pisse," is the catchword, so it is not repeated in the text. The printed hyphen in "ru-" is kept as printed, and the word continues on the next page. "acupicta" and "reciperent" are printed in this form and are left as they are.
